lessonsIntro: Oxwich is a sheltered bay that only surfs in bigger swells, so there is no regular surf school here; it is better known for paddleboarding, kayaking and family watersports.

text: Oxwich Bay faces east into the shelter of the Gower coast, so most of the time the water is calm and shallow, which makes it popular with families, paddleboarders and kayakers. It only produces surfable waves in a big swell, usually best at high water with a north-westerly wind, and on those days it is more suited to experienced surfers than first lessons.

There are no lifeguards at Oxwich, so take care in the water. Jet-skis are banned and boats are expected to be members of Oxwich Boat Club. The beach is privately owned by the Penrice Estate, which runs the large car park on the shorefront. If you want to learn to surf, nearby Caswell Bay, Llangennith or Port Eynon are better bets.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Not a regular learner spot
cards.text: Calm most days, with waves only in big swells. Great for first paddleboard or kayak sessions instead.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: High tide in a big swell
cards.text: Surfers wait for large swells at high water with north-west winds. Flat days suit SUP and kayaks.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: No lifeguards
cards.text: The bay is unpatrolled. Jet-skis are banned and boat users should follow Oxwich Boat Club rules.

hireIntro: Oxwich Watersports runs paddleboard and kayak sessions from the beach, and Gower Stand Up Paddle runs SUP tours from Oxwich.

text: Because Oxwich is usually calm, a stand-up paddleboard or sit-on kayak is the most useful craft for most visitors. When a big swell does wrap in, experienced surfers use their usual shortboards or mid-lengths. For paddling, a summer wetsuit or shortie is plenty in high summer, while spring and autumn sessions call for a full suit and boots.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Bring your own for big swells
cards.text: Surf only works in large swells, so it suits confident surfers with their own boards rather than learners.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 3/2 in summer, 5/4 in winter
cards.text: Gower water peaks at roughly 14-18°C in mid-August and drops to about 8-9°C around March. A 3/2 or 4/3 with boots suits summer; from late autumn to spring go for a 5/4 or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Ideal for SUP and kayak
cards.text: The sheltered, shallow water is good for paddleboarding and kayaking. Jet-skis are not allowed.

shopsIntro: Oxwich has a beach kiosk and a few shops but no surf shop we could confirm.
shopsText: The nearest dedicated surf shop we found is Hot Dog Surf Shop in Kittle, on the road back towards Swansea, which sells boards, wetsuits, bodyboards and accessories and also hires kit. At Oxwich itself there is a beach kiosk plus a nearby restaurant, hotel and other shops for food and beach basics.

lessons.q: Can I learn to surf at Oxwich Bay?
lessons.a: We could not find a surf school that teaches here. Oxwich only gets waves in big swells, so beginners are better off at Caswell or Llangennith.
No. Visit Swansea Bay lists the beach as having no lifeguards, so take extra care.

lessons.q: Can I take a paddleboard lesson at Oxwich?
lessons.a: Oxwich Watersports offers stand-up paddleboarding and kayaking sessions for all ages and levels from Oxwich Beach Hut.

hire.q: What can I hire at Oxwich?
hire.a: Oxwich Watersports offers paddleboard and kayak sessions. We found no surfboard hire on the beach.
There is a large private car park on the shorefront run by the Penrice Estate, with charges and an EV charging point.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop at Oxwich?
shops.a: Not that we could confirm. Hot Dog Surf Shop in Kittle is the nearest dedicated surf shop we found.
